key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXenes are chemically unstable in halide perovskite precursor inks, with I2/polyiodides causing rapid degradation, PbI2 causing slower oxidation, and MAI providing surface passivation and stabilization.
engineering_relevance: The order and composition of perovskite precursors can materially change MXene surface chemistry, so ink formulation and mixing sequence must be controlled for reliable device integration.
method: XPS tracked MXene surface composition after exposure to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
DFT explained the differing adsorption/oxidation pathways for I2, Pb2+, and MAI on Ti3C2Tx surfaces.
Comparative chemical analysis decoupled the roles of each ink constituent in MXene degradation or stabilization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports complementary XPS and DFT results showing rapid I2/polyiodide-driven degradation, slower PbI2-induced oxidation, and MAI-mediated passivation of Ti3C2Tx flakes.
watch_item: MXene behavior depends on precursor order and environment, so implementation requires careful control of ink mixing sequence to avoid unintended degradation.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
